title: Anything but black
caption: The night sky above Paranal Observatory, seen from VISTA
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The plane of the Milky Way shines brightly over Paranal Observatory in this night photograph. The orange speck of Mars sits at left, the magenta patch of the Carina Nebula glows at upper middle, and the starry constellations Scorpius and Orion are also in view. A row of lamps runs through the centre of the frame, lighting the path between the Very Large Telescope and VISTA, the Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for Astronomy, where the photo was taken.
ESO's sites in Chile at Paranal, La Silla and Chajnantor have very little light pollution. Still, the sky over them is rarely pitch-black.

The very sensitive camera also picked up airglow, the faint light given off by Earth's atmosphere, which colours the sky here with deep red and green tones. Airglow means that no observatory on Earth can ever be completely dark, although ESO's sites come close.

understand.summary: This is a night-sky photograph taken at Paranal Observatory with a highly sensitive camera. No camera settings are published.
understand.eye: The sensitive camera records the colours of airglow and faint nebulae that the eye sees only dimly, if at all, at night.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: Astronomer and photographer Yuri Beletsky took the picture as part of the 2016 ESO Fulldome Expedition team. The team travelled to Chile to collect images for the ESO Supernova Planetarium & Visitor Centre.
alt: The Milky Way shining over Paranal Observatory at night, with an orange dot of Mars at left, a magenta nebula at upper middle, a line of small lamps in the centre and a sky tinted red and green by airglow.
